title: MZ Unexplored shadows plugin or deleting tiles through event?

posts.author: CrystalCat
posts.body:
(I would like to apologize for the placement of this thread, it kinda has multiple questions and JS plugin requests were only for MV or so I've heard)
I'm making a dungeon crawler game in RPG maker, and one of the biggest issues I'm running into is how you can see absolutely everything in your game window, no matter where it is, for example, if a player is on one side of a wall, and a surprise enemy or chest is on the other, it's not really a surprise because you can see everything on the other side of the wall.
Ideally, I'd like to have something like
Shattered Pixel Dungeon's
system where you have a line of sight, and everything is much darker outside of that line of sight and while you can see general items and layouts, you can't see any enemies when they're not in your range (pictured below)
Obviously, I realize this is an insane ask for an RPG maker plugin, and likely something that there's been little to no need for, as almost all RPG maker games are turn based, rather than action combat which I'm using for my game. Because of this, I'm very ok with just having something that darkens areas and hides enemies until you get close to it or an event specifies it, and then it's bright forever.
I also understand that even that is likely not a plugin, so my last resort is having a low opacity black tile and putting over the entire map, having it with a built in region ID in tileset editor, then having all my enemies have an event page with no sprite when it's in that region (using checkCollide() ), but not only is that an extremely clunky and possibly laggy option, I have no idea how I would delete that black tile when the player gets close to it (checkRange() is not an option due to it already causing lots of lag, making having it on every tile impossible).
Any plugins or advice or obscure rpg maker script that could help me?

posts.author: Norintha
posts.body: There are a couple plugins that can do a line of sight or fog of war effect. QJ lighting is robust and can do a zillion things, it's all script commands though so if you wanted to use plugin commands you are out of luck. With a lot of work you can do what I did and get it approximated with Community Lighting, although be aware Community Lighting isn't volumetric and you have to do some extensive lightmapping.
